findings.evidence: Page 146, closing paragraph of §7.3.3: "Read every '8-bit' KV figure in this book as FP8 raw byte-halving (one payload byte per K/V element, exactly 2× against FP16)… the realized per-token footprint depends on the engine version… [DERIVED]".
findings.issue: The [DERIVED] tag stands alone without an Axis-1 provenance tag. The Preface evidence boundary (page xv) states: 'A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [canonical scenario][DERIVED].' This paragraph carries only [DERIVED] with no provenance tag. The same pattern recurs: page 137 ends '[1P][FACT] for the configuration; [DERIVED] for the storage' (the second should be [1P][DERIVED]); page 119 in Ch. 6 uses a bare [DERIVED] after a [canonical scenario][DERIVED] pair. Each bare [DERIVED] lacks its provenance counterpart.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the appropriate Axis-1 provenance to every bare [DERIVED] tag: [canonical scenario][DERIVED] for canonical-scenario arithmetic, [1P][DERIVED] for arithmetic on first-party inputs, or [ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED] for non-canonical examples. Apply recurrence sweep across Chs. 6–8.

findings.evidence: Page 145, MXFP4 sensitivity paragraph: "In a 640 GB aggregate pool, a fixed 64 GB runtime reserve leaves 536.75625 GB of KV budget (640 − 39.24375 − 64 = 536.75625 GB)."
findings.issue: The arithmetic checks: 640 − 39.24375 − 64 = 536.75625 ✓. However the prose says the 64 GB runtime reserve 'leaves' 536.76 GB — but the 64 GB is itself one of the three terms being subtracted. The phrase 'a fixed 64 GB runtime reserve leaves 536.76 GB of KV budget' can be read as: (after subtracting weights AND reserve) the KV budget remains. But 640 − 39.24375 = 600.7625, and then − 64 = 536.75625. The subtraction of the 64 GB reserve is correct, but the prose construction 'a fixed 64 GB runtime reserve leaves…' implies the reserve is *being* left (i.e., added back), when in fact it is being subtracted alongside the weights. The standard Ch. 7 formula is 640 − 140 − 64 = 436, where 64 is subtracted separately from weights — here 640 − 39.24 − 64 = 536.76 follows the same pattern, but the English is ambiguous about which term is 'leaving'.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as: 'After subtracting the MXFP4 weights (39.24375 GB) and the fixed 64 GB runtime reserve, the KV budget is 640 − 39.24375 − 64 = 536.75625 GB.'

findings.evidence: Page 136, §7.3.1: "Device capacities are first-party specifications (Intel Arc Pro B70 datasheet, B65 datasheet, Arc Pro B60 datasheet, retrieved 2026-10-28 — post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028, outside the book's 2026-08-30 evidence cutoff, admitted as dated device-capacity documentation and not as a refresh of the August comparison…)".
findings.issue: The source is properly identified and the post-cutoff addendum is properly declared. The sentence is very long (one sentence spanning ~120 words with two parentheticals) — a prose-clarity concern under ASD-STE100. The sentence mixes three topics: (a) which datasheets, (b) retrieval date, (c) addendum policy and scope limit. Breaking into two sentences would improve readability without changing meaning.
findings.fix_instruction: Split into: 'Device capacities come from first-party specifications (Intel Arc Pro B70/B65/B60 datasheets, retrieved 2026-10-28). These datasheets were admitted under post-cutoff addendum v20260913+addendum-20261028 as dated device-capacity documentation; they do not refresh the book's August comparison.'

findings.evidence: Body text: "The figure shows one group's geometry: 8 query heads funnel into a single shared K/V head." The rendered figure (attached image of printed p. 135) draws three groups of eight query heads funnelling into three K/V boxes and carries the label "8 q : 1 KV per group (8 total; 3 shown)".
findings.issue: The prose misdescribes what the figure shows: the drawing is explicitly three of the eight groups (per the figure's own label), not "one group's geometry". The caption's "The head glyphs are schematic" does not license the body text's misreading, and a reader checking the 8:1 ratio against the picture sees three K/V boxes rather than one.
findings.fix_instruction: Change the sentence to "The figure shows three of the eight groups (8 query heads funnelling into one shared K/V head each)", matching the figure's own "8 total; 3 shown" label.

findings.page: PDF p. 154 (printed p. 130); PDF p. 162 (printed p. 138)
findings.evidence: Table 7-1 row: "bytes per parameter (FP16) | 2 | FP16 = 2 bytes/param [1P: IEEE 754 binary16]". Table 7-2 note: "the two vendor constants it divides by, the 640 GB aggregate pool and the 80 GB per-part capacity, are [1P: NVIDIA H100 spec]". Preface, PDF p. 20 (printed p. xvi): "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][FACT], [canonical scenario][DERIVED]... The third axis ... rides with that pair or stands alone."
findings.issue: A third, non-declared label form ("[1P: <source>]") is used in Ch. 7's tables: it fuses a provenance token with a source name and carries no epistemic-status value, so it matches neither a label pair nor a standalone Axis-3 status. It is also inconsistent with the same tables' other rows, which use the declared pair form.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalise to the declared vocabulary: "[1P][FACT] (IEEE 754 binary16)" and "[1P][FACT] (NVIDIA H100 SXM5 datasheet)", moving the source name into the derivation column if preferred.

findings.evidence: "24.9 ÷ 8 ≈ 3.1 GB is the per-rank share at 9.5K, read against a single 80 GB rank's HBM" (Fig 7.5 caption, p. 177); "KV offloading — moving some KV state out of GPU HBM (to host DRAM/SSD), trading capacity against transfer latency" (p. 42); declared convention (p. 22): "the worked examples write 'GPU memory' or 'VRAM' for a capacity and 'HBM' for the technology".
findings.issue: Both instances use 'HBM' for a memory capacity (an 80 GB rank's capacity; a pool that KV state is moved out of), contradicting the Preface's declared usage where 'HBM' names the technology and capacities are written 'GPU memory'/'VRAM' — the exact drift the convention says to avoid.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite as 'read against a single 80 GB rank's GPU memory' and 'moving some KV state out of GPU memory (HBM) to host DRAM/SSD', and sweep the book for remaining capacity-uses of 'HBM'.

findings.evidence: The residency floor is weights + KV: the model’s static parameters plus the context-dependent key/value tensors... In fine-tuning, the floor rises further to weights + gradients + optimizer states, because every parameter update requires its own momentum and velocity vectors (Adam) or per-parameter scaling (LAMB/RMSProp).
findings.issue: Semantic contradiction between front-matter definitions and body-text application: The definition of the fine-tuning residency floor includes 'weights + gradients + optimizer states'. However, in § 7.7 'What We Still Don't Know' (page 149), the text states 'No inference KV cache in a training step; activations excluded from this floor'. This creates semantic ambiguity because a real training step heavily relies on forward pass activations to compute gradients, making the exclusion of both KV and activations mathematically questionable for determining the practical residency floor.
findings.fix_instruction: Clarify in § 7.1 whether the 'residency floor' strictly means persistent memory states and explicitly separate 'Activation Memory' as a dynamic overhead component, rather than burying that exclusion in the 'What We Still Don't Know' section.
